provenance: Saved focused-feedback replay audit. The animation summarizes recorded experiments and results, not raw terminal frames. This run predates later tool-format compatibility and prompt-file separation changes.

evaluations.reason: Correct on 72 brute-force-verified cases. Sieve over multiples with list-indexed freq: measured 0.43s on its worst-case input (1..199999 + 1e6), 0.10s elsewhere — optimal O(M log M) with minimal overhead. Code is direct and clear; only trivial harmless extras (N==0 guard, initial 1e6 alloc).

Correct on all 72 brute-force-verified cases. Same sieve idea but inner loop uses set membership and Counter, slightly looser implementation (0.56s worst case, still well within limits). Minor robustness blemish: blanket try/except pass around the whole solver. Otherwise fine.

Correct on all 72 brute-force-verified cases, but uses per-element trial division up to sqrt(a): O(N*sqrt(maxA)) ~1.9e8 ops. Measured 7.6s on the constraint-legal worst case A=800001..1000000 vs 0.09-0.10s for the sieve solutions (75x gap; original judge timeout was 6s, so it only passed because tests missed this case). Overhead is clearly avoidable; also has dead code (unused set(A)).

review_notes: Original outcomes remain unchanged; extra experiments inform quality weights only.
Each pressure input was measured once in this replay; timing ratios are not a stable speedup benchmark.
The large trial-division cost is supported; the model claim about why original tests passed and its optimality claim are not established.
The exact 0.95 vs 0.85 distinction between the two sieve solutions is debatable; both can reasonably receive the same high tier.
Six format errors recovered before successful submission; constrained JSON decoding was not used.
